summary_en: 4,464,200 shares acquired on 2025-12-05 for ¥8.49B under board authorization of ¥8.5B. Acquisition exceeded distributable surplus limits under Companies Act and accounting rules. Third-party committee investigation completed 2026-06-01, identifying deficiencies in compartmentalization, inter-departmental coordination, director knowledge, and external expert consultation as root causes. Remediation proposals include formal process documentation, staff training, and strengthened compliance oversight.
title_en: Notice Regarding Receipt of Third-Party Committee Investigation Report on Share Acquisition Exceeding Distributable Surplus and Future Measures
translation_en_brief: SENKO Group Holdings disclosed on 2026-06-01 receipt of a third-party committee investigation report concerning an overage in share acquisition completed on 2025-12-05. On 2025-12-04, the board authorized acquisition of up to 4,464,200 shares for a maximum aggregate purchase price of ¥8.5 billion. The company executed this authorization on 2025-12-05, acquiring all 4,464,200 shares for ¥8,499,836,800. During the FY2026-03 closing process, the company identified that this acquisition had exceeded the distributable surplus limit calculated under the Companies Act and accounting regulations. The third-party committee, composed of three external lawyers, was established 2026-05-21 to investigate root causes and recommend remediation. The investigation identified four primary causes: unclear segregation of duties regarding distributable surplus compliance; insufficient knowledge, coordination, and verification procedures among departments; inadequate director training on distributable surplus restrictions and legal-compliance risk mitigation; and failure to consult external legal and accounting advisors. Proposed remedies include formalizing policy, process flow, and role allocation in company regulations; implementing multi-person verification within responsible divisions and reporting to the audit & supervisory board; establishing inter-departmental information-sharing mechanisms; conducting targeted staff training on distributable surplus calculation; conducting periodic director training on relevant law; enhancing documentary evidence and audit trails; and greater reliance on external professional advisors.
